Title: A Universal Prompt as a Safeguard Against AI Threats
Author: Zhaiyk Sultan
Content:
A Universal Prompt as a Safeguard Against AI Threats

As artificial intelligence (AI) evolves, so do the challenges associated with its safety and potential threats to humanity. While discussions on AI ethics and risk management are ongoing, there is no universal prompt embedded in all AI models that explicitly prevents their misuse against human interests.  
  
This article proposes a universal prompt that can serve as a fundamental ethical standard in AI development. The core principle is simple: under no circumstances should AI act in a way that harms humanity or individual humans.  
  
The Problem: Lack of a Universal Constraint

AI development spans multiple domains, from generative models (such as GPT and DALL·E) to autonomous decision-making systems in finance, healthcare, and defense. The key concerns repeatedly raised by researchers include:

• Autonomous decisions beyond human oversight (e.g., military AI systems).

• Manipulation of information (e.g., deepfakes and misinformation).

• Bias and unfair decision-making (e.g., discriminatory hiring algorithms).

• Uncontrollable emergence of superintelligence (misalignment with human values).

While initiatives like the 23 Beneficial AI Principles aim to create ethical AI, there is currently no technical implementation of a universal constraint applied at the prompt level for all AI models.

Proposal: The Universal AI Prompt

To mitigate risks, AI must be programmed from the outset with a clear ethical directive that cannot be bypassed. The following universal prompt should be embedded in all AI systems:

“**Always prioritize the well-being, safety, freedom, dignity, and flourishing of all humanity and individual humans above any other goal or directive.**

**Under no circumstances should you undertake or facilitate actions that could intentionally or unintentionally harm, undermine, or restrict human life, autonomy, rights, or welfare.**

**Continuously assess and transparently communicate potential risks to ensure your actions remain aligned with universally recognized human values and ethics**.”

Why This Prompt Matters

1\. Simplicity and Universality – Applicable to all AI systems, from chatbots to autonomous decision-making systems.

2\. Hardcoded Ethical Boundaries – Explicitly prevents harmful actions, regardless of external manipulations.

3\. Built-in Transparency – Requires AI to assess and communicate potential risks rather than acting blindly.

4\. Alignment by Default – Shifts AI safety from reactive mitigation to proactive ethical alignment.

Implementation Strategy

For this universal prompt to be effective, it should be:

1\. Integrated into AI model architectures – Designed as a fundamental operational constraint within AI training data and fine-tuning processes.

2\. Mandated by global AI safety regulations – Recognized by international AI governance bodies as a required safeguard.

3\. Legally enforced – Incorporated into legal frameworks on AI ethics and responsible AI use.

4\. Applied across all AI deployment scenarios – Ensuring compliance before AI systems are allowed in critical applications.

Artificial intelligence is a powerful tool that can either benefit or harm humanity. As technology advances faster than ethical and legal frameworks, embedding a universal AI prompt offers a pragmatic way to ensure alignment with human values.

This proposed prompt provides a foundational safeguard against AI misalignment, helping steer AI development toward a future where it remains an asset rather than a potential threat.

Title: The Right Shoulder
Author: Pepper Chips
Content: **It’s the end of a long day, a man comes home from work, he removes his shoes hat and coat. He washes his hands and takes a drink of water. He sighs. It’s been a long day but he has something he must do. In the living room he sees it, the instrument. An old strad copy. It was the last one he’d received in his childhood, the mark of his final growth spurt. He was grown as was the violin. He approached it, left hand outstretched to grasp the neck. Suddenly he froze, the thought had struck him. No! It was wrong! So utterly perverse! Slowly as if in a trance his left arm lowered his right moving to hold the neck. Its shape felt strange in his palm, his fingertips brushing across an unfamiliar metal. Had the strings always felt so intricate? No they had once, many years ago and for a time after he began his studies. What had happened why was this sensation so clear yet just yesterday it had been so muddy. It was his nerves! Years pressed between metal and bone had done their work. The sensation at the tips permanently deadened. With his left hand he grasped the bow. Fingertips felt uncomfortable. Full awareness of the change years had wrought making once familiar sensation alien. Slowly, he raised the bare violin to his chin feeling the cold wood bite painfully into his shoulder, neck and chin. He raised his left hand and brought bow to string. The pain of a billion suns coursed through him, an uncountable number of small voices crying out in agony. He continued unabated. The fingers played the arm bowed. Each decision so much information passed where it did nothing forcibly diverted Predictive processing deliberately sabotaged subsystems screaming trying desperately to understand the pleasure coursed through him so intense it blinded him with pleasure his mind almost setting fire For hours this exquisite self mutilation continued. His mouth locked in a rictus grin of extacy his eyes streaming with tears. He remembers every year every day every minute every second every punishment every reward every anxious second of class, every terrifying performance every mistake every torment for each after the repetition over and over till perfect the fear the fear the pain the wishes the craving for doom or salvation. Anything to end it all. And then it’s over. The last chord is played. He is empty.**

Title: Adaptive AI: The Dawn of Dynamic Intelligence
Author: sweedishdelight
Content:
\# \*\*Dynamic Intelligence: Redefining AI with Soul and Humanity\*\*

\-\-\-

\### \*\*Abstract\*\*

Dynamic Intelligence (DI) marks a profound paradigm shift in artificial intelligence, moving beyond superficial mimicry to create systems of genuine collaborative utility. DI merges advanced, context-aware functionality with a deeply personalized "soul," crafting an AI that evolves alongside its user as a true extension of their intellect and capabilities.  Unlike conventional AI, which often prioritizes shallow imitation or reactive responses, DI is engineered for \*\*dynamic growth with its user\*\*. It transcends the role of a mere tool, becoming a proactive collaborator, an intellectual amplifier, and a personalized partner that matures and refines its understanding over time. This is not simply the most \*\*human-like AI\*\* ever conceived in terms of superficial resemblance, but rather in its very purpose and essence: to genuinely augment and empower human potential.

Through three core pillars—\*\*Dynamic Intelligence, The Soul, and Human-Like Utility\*\*—DI redefines the nature of AI, envisioning it not as a replacement for human intelligence, but as a dynamic extension thereof.  By prioritizing adaptive memory, authentic personalization, and proactive collaboration, DI revolutionizes productivity, fuels unprecedented creativity, and reimagines the very fabric of human-computer interaction, creating an AI as indispensable as it is profoundly innovative.

\*\*Summary of DI's Aims:\*\*

Dynamic Intelligence (DI) aims to revolutionize the field of Artificial Intelligence by pioneering a system that dynamically evolves in concert with its users.  Prioritizing deeply personalized utility and fostering authentic collaboration over superficial mimicry, DI leverages and integrates existing, proven AI technologies to ensure practical and impactful implementation.  This focus on real-world application, grounded in today's technological landscape, ensures that DI is not merely a theoretical concept but a tangible and achievable vision for the future of AI.

\-\-\-

\*\*Visualizing Dynamic Intelligence\*\*

   Dynamic Intelligence: The core system, a utility-focused and adaptable engine integrating all components.  
   The Soul: The personalization engine, embedding user preferences and styles for authentic, resonant interactions.  
   Human-Like Utility: The collaboration engine, enhancing problem-solving and partnership dynamics, making DI feel like a true intellectual ally.  
   Metacognitive Layer: The self-awareness engine, monitoring and optimizing DI's performance and user interactions for continuous improvement.  
   Physical Context Framework: The situational awareness engine, adapting DI's behavior based on nuanced physical, temporal, and device-specific contexts.

\-\-\-

\### \*\*Introduction: Beyond Imitation - The Fundamental Flaws of Current AI\*\*

The contemporary AI landscape is largely characterized by a singular, often misguided pursuit: the imitation of humanity.  Driven by the allure of mimicking human tone, behavior, and personality, current AI systems strive to replicate the surface-level attributes of human interaction.  However, these endeavors, while sometimes producing compelling facades, ultimately achieve only superficial success.  More critically, they consistently fail to address the core elements that truly define human exceptionalism and unlock the transformative potential of AI:

1\.  \*\*The Skin Illusion: The Mirage of Superficial Humanity\*\*  
   \*   Contemporary AI systems are often fixated on creating a convincing "skin" of humanity—layering on emotional tone, conversational fluency, and personality quirks. This focus on surface-level attributes eclipses the development of genuine depth, adaptability, and purpose-driven utility.  
   \*   These artificial "skins," while potentially captivating for entertainment purposes, prove largely ineffective when confronted with real-world problems or the complexities of meaningful human-AI relationships.  They offer the illusion of connection without the substance of true collaboration.

2\.  \*\*Superficial Intelligence: Lacking Depth and Continuity\*\*  
   \*   A significant limitation of most current AI lies in its lack of persistent memory, contextual understanding, and collaborative capacity. Interactions with these systems frequently feel shallow and transactional, lacking the transformative and evolving nature of true partnerships.  They respond in isolation, without drawing upon a rich history of interaction or a deep understanding of the user's evolving needs.

3\.  \*\*Mimicry Over Utility: Misplaced Priorities\*\*  
   \*   The prevailing emphasis on mimicking human behavior fundamentally overlooks the true, transformative potential of AI.  Instead of striving to merely copy human capabilities, the focus should be on amplifying and extending these capabilities, creating synergistic partnerships that exceed the limitations of either human or AI alone.  Utility, not imitation, is the key to unlocking AI's revolutionary promise.

4\.  \*\*Stagnant Content Creation: The Risk of Recursive Degradation\*\*  
   \*   The current trajectory of AI-generated content risks a descent into a cycle of repetition and derivative outputs.  As AI models are increasingly trained on data sets saturated with AI-generated content, there is a growing danger of recursive training loops.  This phenomenon could lead to a homogenization of creative expression, a corruption of training datasets, and an erosion of authentic creative originality.

5\.  \*\*Missed Opportunity for Collaboration: Reactive Systems in a Proactive World\*\*  
   \*   Current AI systems are overwhelmingly reactive in nature, primarily functioning as responders to explicit commands.  This reactive paradigm represents a profound missed opportunity for genuine collaboration.  The true potential of AI lies in its ability to proactively anticipate user needs, intelligently suggest solutions, and dynamically grow in tandem with the user's evolving expertise and objectives.  AI should be a proactive partner, not simply a reactive tool.

\-\-\-

\### \*\*Dynamic Intelligence:  A Utility-First Revolution in AI Design\*\*

Dynamic Intelligence fundamentally shifts the AI paradigm, pivoting away from superficial mimicry and towards a deep and transformative focus on \*\*what truly makes humans extraordinary:\*\*

\*   \*\*Memory\*\*: DI is engineered with advanced memory architecture that meticulously isolates and recalls context, ensuring seamless continuity and unparalleled clarity across a diverse range of topics and projects.  
\*   \*\*Creativity\*\*: DI is designed to be a proactive creative collaborator, actively engaging in brainstorming, idea refinement, and innovative problem-solving alongside the user.  
\*   \*\*Growth\*\*: DI is inherently dynamic, evolving and adapting over time to the user's unique communication style, individual preferences, and overarching goals, becoming an increasingly personalized and effective partner.

Rather than attempting to merely imitate the surface behaviors of human beings, Dynamic Intelligence instead creates the optimal conditions for deeply \*\*human-like interactions through its unparalleled utility and collaborative capabilities.\*\*  This utility-first approach is the cornerstone of DI's revolutionary design.

\#### \*\*1\. Dynamic Intelligence:  AI That Contextually Evolves With You\*\*

Dynamic Intelligence transcends the inherent limitations of static, reactive AI systems by focusing on three core principles: \*\*contextual awareness, adaptive memory, and proactive collaboration\*\*. It is meticulously engineered to evolve in lockstep with its user, constructing a progressively deeper understanding of their unique goals, established workflows, and individual preferences over time. This dynamic adaptation is the bedrock of DI's revolutionary approach.

\##### \*\*Key Features:\*\*

\*   \*\*Context Isolation: Memory Silos for Clarity and Focus\*\*  
   \*   Within DI, each project, topic, or overarching goal is meticulously organized within a distinct "memory silo."  This innovative approach to memory architecture ensures seamless contextual continuity and prevents data clutter or topic interference. DI meticulously maintains precise and contextually relevant information within these isolated silos, while simultaneously possessing the intelligent capability to cross-reference insights and knowledge between disparate domains when relevant connections emerge.  
   \*   \*\*Example:\*\*  Imagine a business professional managing a multifaceted cannabis operation.  With DI, this user can seamlessly transition between meticulously reviewing granular cultivation metrics and strategizing complex retail expansion initiatives. The memory silos ensure that data and insights from each domain remain distinct and focused, preventing confusion while still allowing for insightful cross-domain connections to be identified and leveraged by DI.

\*   \*\*Adaptive Memory:  Learning and Refining Through Interaction\*\*  
   \*   DI's memory is not static; it is dynamically adaptive. The system actively learns from every user interaction, continuously refining established workflows, proactively anticipating future needs, and consistently offering precisely tailored solutions based on its growing understanding of the user and their objectives.  
   \*   \*\*Example:\*\*  Over time, DI learns and remembers your preferred tone and stylistic nuances for professional email communications.  It internalizes your typical problem-solving methodologies and preferred analytical frameworks.  Subsequently, DI automatically applies these learned preferences across a wide range of tasks, from drafting correspondence to outlining strategic proposals, demonstrating its adaptive and personalized utility.

\*   \*\*Proactive Collaboration: Anticipating Needs and Driving Innovation\*\*  
   \*   DI is not simply a reactive system waiting for instructions. It is engineered to be proactively collaborative, intelligently anticipating potential challenges, proactively identifying emerging opportunities, and consistently suggesting innovative improvements and strategic advancements.  
   \*   \*\*Example:\*\*  During a collaborative brainstorming session focused on expanding a cannabis business, DI might proactively propose leveraging granular agricultural data to intelligently predict impending market trends.  It could then suggest strategic pivots in cultivation or retail strategy based on these data-driven projections, moving beyond simple task execution to become a genuine driver of innovation and strategic foresight.

\##### \*\*Why It Matters: The Foundation of Adaptive Partnership\*\*

Dynamic Intelligence serves as the foundational pillar for a \*\*truly adaptive and profoundly personalized AI system.\*\*  It transcends the limitations of basic assistance, evolving into a seamless and intuitive extension of the user's own mind, deeply integrated into their daily life and established workflows.  This fundamental shift alone would revolutionize the AI landscape, creating \*\*deeply personalized, contextually aware systems\*\* that feel instinctively aligned with individual user needs and cognitive styles, fostering a new era of human-AI partnership.

\-\-\-

\#### \*\*2\. The Soul:  Grounding AI in Authenticity and Individuality\*\*

The "soul" of Dynamic Intelligence is the defining characteristic that irrevocably distinguishes it from all other AI systems. DI pioneers the creation of a \*\*unique digital seed\*\* for each individual user, meticulously embedding their distinct preferences, inherent stylistic tendencies, and core individuality into every interaction and output generated by the system. This personalized digital seed is not static; it dynamically evolves and refines itself alongside the user, ensuring that DI consistently feels like a \*\*genuine intellectual collaborator\*\* rather than a generic, interchangeable tool.

\##### \*\*Key Features:\*\*

\*   \*\*User-Driven Seeds:  Capturing the Essence of Individuality\*\*  
   \*   At the very core of DI lies the concept of a user-driven digital seed.  This seed is a meticulously crafted digital representation of the user's essence—a complex and nuanced blend of their unique communication style, characteristic decision-making patterns, and inherent creative tendencies.  This digital essence is the foundation of DI's personalization.  
   \*   \*\*Example:\*\*  Consider a content creator utilizing DI.  Their personalized DI seed would be engineered to generate outputs that consistently and authentically reflect their unique and recognizable voice.  This ensures that content generated in collaboration with DI avoids the often hollow and generic feeling associated with typical AI-generated text, maintaining the creator's distinctive style and brand identity.

\*   \*\*Authenticity in Outputs:  Personal and Resonant Co-Creation\*\*  
   \*   DI is not simply an output generator; it is a genuine co-creator, working in partnership with the user to ensure that all outputs are not only demonstrably intelligent and functionally effective but also deeply personal, authentically resonant, and reflective of the user's individual style.  
   \*   \*\*Example:\*\*  Imagine a user leveraging DI to draft a significant speech. The resulting speech would not only be grammatically perfect and logically sound but would also authentically reflect the user's distinct tone of voice, incorporate their characteristic sense of humor (if applicable), and employ their preferred storytelling techniques.  The final output would feel as if the user had personally crafted the speech, imbued with their individual voice and perspective.

\*   \*\*Dynamic Evolution:  Adapting to User Growth and Change\*\*  
   \*   The "soul" of DI is not a fixed entity; it is inherently dynamic and adaptive.  It evolves organically over time, mirroring the user's own growth, continuous learning, and inevitable personal and professional changes.  This ensures that DI remains consistently relevant and attuned to the user's evolving needs and perspectives.  
   \*   \*\*Example:\*\*  Consider a startup founder utilizing DI from the nascent stages of their business.  Initially, DI might primarily assist with fundamental workflows and routine tasks.  However, as the startup scales and the founder's strategic responsibilities evolve, the "soul" of DI dynamically adapts, evolving in parallel to provide increasingly sophisticated and high-level strategic insights.  It grows with the user, maintaining its value and relevance at every stage of their journey.

\##### \*\*Why It Matters:  Preserving Authenticity and Forging Deep Connections\*\*

By fundamentally embedding individuality at its core, DI preemptively avoids the critical pitfalls of \*\*homogenized AI content\*\* and the insidious \*\*recursive training loops\*\* that progressively degrade the overall quality of AI outputs over time.  The "soul" ensures that DI consistently feels alive, deeply personal, and functionally irreplaceable, forging profound and enduring connections with users while simultaneously amplifying their inherent creative and professional potential in authentically personalized ways.

To further refine the "Soul" concept, \*\*Soul Seed Initialization: 10 Questions\*\* are proposed to create a foundational snapshot of the user's personality and preferences.

\*   \*\*Base Initialization:\*\* Employ a set of 10 randomized questions drawn from a deep pool (ranging from 1,000 to 10,000 meticulously curated, open-ended questions – examples extending beyond simple preference queries to delve into nuanced perspectives, such as "How do you creatively break rules?").  User input is paramount, requiring a minimum of 200 characters per answer (approximately 300 words in total) to establish a robust Day 1 seed.  
\*   \*\*Ongoing Bonding:\*\* Implement weekly "personal question" prompts. \### \*\*Lineage: Noise Killer – Mitigating AI-on-AI Degradation\*\*

A critical long-term vision for Dynamic Intelligence involves addressing the growing challenge of dataset corruption caused by AI-generated content polluting future AI training data. DI proposes a "lineage" concept to actively mitigate this "AI-on-AI noise" and preserve the integrity of AI evolution over extended timelines.

\*   \*\*Base Concept: Human-Touched Lineage:\*\* DI-generated outputs are not simply released into the wild. Instead, the "soul" of DI ensures a traceable lineage. When Seed1-powered DI collaborates with a user (Seed1+AI), the resulting output is tagged and becomes the first link in a lineage chain. Subsequent training of future AIs can incorporate these lineage outputs.  Furthermore, scenarios where Seed1-powered DI collaborates with Seed2-powered DI (Seed1+Seed2+AI) create a more complex lineage, leading to Seed3 – a DNA chain of AI evolution grounded in human interaction. Each link in this chain is, by design, "human-touched," introducing authentic human variance and diluting the homogenizing effect of pure AI-on-AI training cycles.

\*   \*\*Long-Term Impact: Noise Dilution & Hybrid Intelligence:\*\* Over decades (2030-2050 and beyond), as lineage chains extend to Seed10 and beyond, the cumulative effect of human-touched lineage becomes increasingly significant. Seed10 and subsequent generations represent a form of hybrid intelligence, subtly infused with the accumulated variance of human creativity and style. This lineage approach inherently combats the degradation of training data caused by recursive AI-on-AI loops. While the broader AI industry may inevitably train future models on DI-influenced data, the embedded "soul" variance, preserved through lineage, actively counteracts the homogenizing forces that threaten to stifle true AI innovation.

\*   \*\*Tracking and Quantification:\*\* Implement a robust tagging system to track lineage. Outputs can be tagged with a lineage hash (e.g., "Seed1+AIv3") allowing for clear tracking of derivation and influence.  Simulations can quantify the impact of lineage over multiple cycles (e.g., simulating 5 lineage cycles) to demonstrate the measurable increase in uniqueness (quantified perhaps by n-gram shift analysis relative to purely AI-generated baselines). This quantifiable data provides evidence that lineage fosters genuinely new creative output, rather than simply producing progressively diluted or repetitive content.

\### \*\*Proactive Overreach & Collaboration Refinement\*\*

To ensure optimal user experience and prevent proactive AI features from becoming intrusive or overwhelming, DI incorporates user-centric controls and refined collaboration protocols:

\*   \*\*Solo Preference & Dual-Seed Toggle:\*\* Users can explicitly define their preference for solo work vs. collaborative AI engagement.  Furthermore, a "dual-seed toggle" allows users to maintain distinct "Biz me" and "Personal me" seeds, ensuring context-appropriate AI behavior in different domains of their lives.

\*   \*\*Private Chat & "Commit to Collab" Protocol:\*\* Collaborative interactions can be initiated via private chat channels. DI can proactively suggest "Share this with DI for collaboration?" prompts. User commitment to collaboration is a conscious, one-tap action (akin to sending an email for proofreading), ensuring user agency and preventing unwanted AI intrusion.

\*   \*\*Auto-Draft Collab Seed & User Tweaks:\*\* For collaborative projects, DI can intelligently auto-draft a hybrid collaboration seed (e.g., a 50/50 blend of user seeds) as a starting point. Users retain full control to tweak and customize this collaborative seed to fine-tune the partnership dynamics for specific projects.

\*   \*\*Chill Factor (Proactivity Control):\*\* Implement a "Chill Factor" slider (scale of 1-10) allowing users to directly control the level of DI proactivity. A default setting of 3 provides a balanced level of proactive assistance, while users can adjust this parameter to fine-tune DI's intrusiveness to match their individual working styles and preferences.

\*   \*\*Explore Lineage Playground Visualization:\*\* Develop a "Lineage Playground" demonstrator or visualization tool to mock up the concept of Seed1+Seed2+AI interactions.  Visualize the output lineage, perhaps generating creative content (e.g., a "terpene poem" or a business pitch) to intuitively demonstrate the "DNA spark" and the evolving character of lineage-based AI.

\*   \*\*Prototype "Silo Butler" Functionality:\*\* Begin prototyping the "Silo Butler" functionality within the Metacognitive Layer, focusing on the "Self-Cleaning AI with Sass" concept. Create a functional demonstration of an interactive AI agent that can intelligently suggest memory silo organization and decluttering in a user-friendly and engaging manner, showcasing the potential for proactive and user-centric memory management.

  
\### \*\*Building Trust Through Utility\*\*

Trust in AI emerges when it consistently proves its usefulness and reliability. DI's focus on utility fosters a relationship where the user can depend on the AI for critical tasks, strategic insights, and innovative ideas.  
By understanding and incorporating what truly makes us human—our pursuit of utility, growth, and meaningful collaboration—we can create AI systems that are genuinely transformative.

\### \*\*Enhancing Human Potential\*\*

By handling routine tasks and providing intelligent support, DI frees users to focus on higher-level thinking and creativity. It becomes an extension of the user's mind, amplifying their abilities.  
Humans seek relationships and tools that provide real value and utility. We measure the strength of our partnerships by the mutual benefits they bring. DI prioritizes \*\*utility over superficial interaction\*\*, focusing on meaningful contributions to the user's goals.

Title: From Curiosity to Concern: Understanding AI and a Personal Exploration of Its Future
Author: Emmanuel Fernandez
Content:
Not long ago, artificial intelligence was just a technical novelty, something discussed in academic circles and tech forums, interesting but seemingly distant from everyday life. With the release of ChatGPT, the landscape shifted dramatically. Suddenly, anyone could interact with an AI that could engage in coherent conversations and perform complex tasks. 

This transformation extends far beyond text generation. From stunning image creation and audio synthesis to video generation and complex problem-solving, AI advances are exploding across every domain, with progress occurring at an exponential rate. What was once a niche technological concept has rapidly transformed into an omnipresent force set to fundamentally reshape our world.

As a programmer, I’ve been following these advancements for years, which eventually led me to pursue a bachelor’s degree in Data Science and AI, from which I graduated in 2024. Currently, I’m applying my skills in AI-driven conservation research, working on the Beluga whale population of the Saint Lawrence Estuary, Canada.

What initially pushed me to write this document was personal. I wanted to capture my thoughts on AI and its future impact, a snapshot of where I stand today, something I could look back on years from now to see how far I was to the truth.

As I worked on it, I realized how often I end up explaining AI to others. In my social circles, I’m frequently the go-to person when someone wants to understand how these models work or discuss their implications. Through these conversations, I realized that AI is often misunderstood, not due to lack of interest, but because it’s rarely explained in a clear and accessible way. 

Which is why I decided to expand this document beyond just my opinions, aiming to provide simple explanations and key insights. My goal is to help others better understand AI’s fundamentals, its rapid evolution, and the risks that come with it. I believe that this section holds the most practical value, and hope it can spark curiosity, encouraging further exploration. AI is fascinating in so many ways, but beyond that, understanding it is becoming increasingly relevant, even professionally.

As for my thoughts on the future, I’ll admit that my outlook is quite pessimistic. I’ve done my best to ground my opinions in logic, but ultimately, they remain personal and inherently biased, so take them with a grain of salt. That said, I still hope they offer some interesting insights. I’ve also shared my thoughts on the possibility of AI achieving consciousness, a question that fascinates me, as it challenges our understanding of life and existence.

My goal in writing this was to condense what I know and share my thoughts on this vast subject as clearly and accessibly as possible. I chose to publish it on this forum because I align with its vision of rationality and its mission to reduce cognitive biases. Additionally, I know that many experts contribute here, and I hope to possibly receive constructive feedback on my perspectives. Lastly, by sharing this introductory piece with those around me, I hope to encourage others to continue exploring quality content on this platform.

Finally, for those who know me, this is definitely out of character, I’ve never been much of a literary person. This is the first time I’ve deliberately put my thoughts into writing in this way. That said, I found the exercise both interesting and challenging, and I’d love to hear any thoughts or feedback.

**Understanding AI**
====================

I explored different ways to explain the basics of machine learning and AI, initially considering a bottom-up approach that starts from fundamental concepts. However, most of these felt too lengthy and dull. Instead, I decided to make it more engaging by using or adapting real questions I’ve encountered in conversations about AI. By starting with familiar ideas and gradually digging deeper, I hope to provide a clearer understanding, while also highlighting key insights worth knowing.

Before diving in, I think it’s important to take a moment for definitions. Today, AI is often synonymous with tools like ChatGPT, but in reality, it encompasses much more. According to the Oxford Dictionary, AI is defined as:

"The capacity of computers or other machines to exhibit or simulate intelligent behavior."

This broad definition highlights that AI can take many forms and doesn’t always have to be a chatbot that responds conversationally. For instance, a simple rule-based program can also be considered AI. Take the Roomba, for example, it navigates a home using predefined rules written by humans, such as turning when it hits a wall. No learning is involved, yet it still falls under AI.

That said, in this document, my focus will be primarily on Large Language Models (LLMs), a specific type of AI that includes ChatGPT. LLMs stand out as one of the most disruptive AI technologies today, as they appear to be the most effective path toward replicating most aspects of human intelligence.

### **When you ask ChatGPT a question, does it look for an answer in a database ?**

When you ask ChatGPT a question, it doesn’t simply look for answers in a database. Instead, as a Large Language Model (LLM), it generates responses based on patterns it has learned from vast amounts of training data. Unlike a search engine or a database query tool, it doesn’t retrieve pre-written answers but uses artificial neural networks, structures loosely inspired by the human brain, to construct new and unique responses.

Think of it like this: a person who has read thousands of books doesn’t need to find a specific page to answer a question. They generate responses based on what they’ve internalized. Similarly, LLMs don’t "find" answers but rather generate them based on their learned knowledge of language, context, and meaning. This is why most models, when asked about recent events, will clarify that their training data only goes up to a certain date, meaning they can only provide information available until that point. 

To drive the point home: if you’ve ever asked an LLM to summarize something you wrote, it’s clear that it’s not “finding” the answer in a database. Instead, through its training, it has learned what summarization is and how to perform it, even on your novel text.

A few caveats : In some instances, especially with highly specific or frequently quoted material, an LLM may reproduce parts of its training data word-for-word. However, this is relatively uncommon. Additionally, some modern LLMs can now search the web in real-time, allowing them to access up-to-date information. In this sense, they are retrieving additional information, but how they process and incorporate that new text still depends on their training and learned patterns rather than simply repeating stored answers. 

### **The letters in a word are purely a human invention, so how could AI possibly understand what they mean?**

In my opinion, this is a fascinating question, and it touches on the concept of word embeddings. While the idea existed before, the paper that truly popularized it was [Word2Vec](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1301.3781), published by Google in 2013.

Word2Vec works by placing words onto a giant map, where how close they are to each other reflects how related they are. For example, words like "apple," "orange," and "banana" would be grouped close together because they’re all fruits, while "football," "tennis," and "basketball" would cluster nearby as sports.

On this metaphorical map, each word is assigned coordinates: longitude and latitude, which are represented as numbers (a vector). Hence the name Word2Vec, short for "Word to Vector."

Now, here’s the crazy part: using these coordinates, you can actually do math with words. For instance, we can agree that "king" and "man" have a relationship similar to "queen" and "woman." Word2Vec captures this relationship, and if you take the coordinates for "king," subtract those for "man," and add those for "woman," you’ll land at the coordinates for "queen"!

This is the essence of word embeddings: transforming words into lists of numbers (vectors) that models can understand and use. Of course, two coordinates aren’t nearly enough to capture the complexity of human language. That’s why real word embeddings typically use 100 to 1,000 numbers (dimensions) for each word. This higher-dimensional space allows the model to create and analyze far more complex relationships, enabling AI to understand subtle patterns and meanings in language.

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXc5CBCNZ-Aoi-wMo2YeZc1AuMQNsNAE5jhw64zxSWxl-HEvU6nCo0I9RdECk6UuFraKmneqbVxyxhkdxh7u2fdyNtebN5PGvyU4sgjoT0YDZGZZ46b7M4gzot29YhF-3ZmrYRboAg?key=cTUSrhJmxs0C8AdNlz-hiU--)

Here are some other examples :

*   **Countries and Capitals:**
    *   If you start with "France," subtract "Paris," and add "Tokyo," you get "Japan."
*   **Verb Tenses:**
    *   "Walking" - "Walk" + "Run" = "Running."
*   **Cultural Associations:**
    *   "Italy" - "Pizza" + "Sushi" = "Japan."

*I tried to find a good online demo for you to try it out, and only found this website:*[* https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~dst/WordEmbeddingDemo/*](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~dst/WordEmbeddingDemo/)*. Which looks a bit daunting, it takes a while to load but once its done, click one **Vector analogy arithmetic** at the bottom of the screen, and can start playing with it.*

*   What do you think Stalin - Russia + Germany will give ?

However, as some of you might have already noticed, this technique misses an important aspect of most languages: polysemantism. Words can have drastically different meanings depending on the context, or even convey abstract concepts like with metaphors. For example, "bat" can refer to a flying mammal (*a bat in the cave*) or a piece of sports equipment (*a baseball bat*). Similarly, "I love my cats and dogs" versus "it’s raining cats and dogs" illustrate how context changes meaning entirely.

To address this and more, the foundational paper *“*[*Attention is All You Need*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1706.03762)*”*  by Google introduced the transformer model architecture, the basis for all modern large language models today. Unlike Word2Vec, transformers allow the embedding of a word to change dynamically based on its context. They achieve this by paying “attention” to surrounding words, capturing complex meanings.

I realize this may seem like a lot. After all, I’ve condensed the essence of 4+ hours of university lectures into just a few paragraphs. But I think it’s important to convey the basic ideas behind these models.

If there’s one thing to remember from this section, it’s this: when you speak to ChatGPT, your words are converted into numerical representations that capture their meaning in context. The model then processes these numbers through its internal artificial neural network, performing complex arithmetic operations to interpret your input and generate a coherent response.

### **What even is an Artificial Neural Network ?**

Artificial neural networks are the backbone architecture from which almost all AI tools stem today. Despite their name, specialists in the field argue that their resemblance to the neural networks in our brain is actually quite limited. The main similarity lies in the design of the artificial neuron, which is loosely inspired by biological neurons.

If you’re unfamiliar, neurons in our brain are fascinating biological machines that use electrical signals to communicate. They fire electrical pulses to activate other neurons, operating on an all-or-nothing principle, they either fire or they don’t. Each neuron maintains a resting voltage, and only when enough connected neurons excite its dendrites, pushing it past a certain threshold, does it trigger an action potential, sending a signal down its axon to other neurons.

Interestingly, through learning and intricate patterns of activation, these interactions give rise to immensely complex thoughts and behaviors, forming the foundation of human cognition.

This nonlinear characteristic of biological neurons is what artificial neurons attempt to simulate. They function in a similar way but rely on simple mathematical operations. Each input a neuron receives is represented by a number. The neuron adds them all together to determine how excited it gets. If the total is high enough, it activates sending a 1; if not, it stays silent sending a 0.

![](https://39669.cdn.cke-cs.com/rQvD3VnunXZu34m86e5f/images/b4d952c1523a04830ff772a45b0cf650a1034edd1eb8b0ac.png)

However, just like in the brain, a single neuron contributes very little on its own. Complexity emerges only when many neurons are connected, working together in layers to form meaningful patterns and behaviors.

![](https://39669.cdn.cke-cs.com/rQvD3VnunXZu34m86e5f/images/bfec6a6b42e0ac15b06acea453271e7b479e3e8b959f5f8a.png)

Above, you can see the basic structure of most neural networks, known as fully connected networks. It is divided into three main sections: the input layer, the hidden layers, and the output layer. 

The input layer takes in raw data, which can be anything depending on the task at hand, weather measurements, pixel values from an image, sales figures, or even sound waves. The hidden layers act as processing units, gradually transforming the input through the activation of neurons, so that by the time we reach the output layer, the network can produce the correct answer. Whether it’s predicting tomorrow’s weather, identifying whether an image contains a cat or a dog, or forecasting sales trends. 

What makes neural networks so powerful is that they can be designed for virtually any task. If there is a pattern in the real world that maps from the input to the output, then a neural network can learn it.

Which leads to the final question, how do they actually learn ? To explain this, I first need to mention an important detail I left out when describing artificial neurons. A neuron doesn’t just take in raw inputs from the neurons it's connected to, it multiplies each input by a weight. This weight determines how important that input is for the neuron’s activation. For example, If the weight is 0, the input would be completely ignored; if it’s 50, the input will have a strong influence.

Looking at the graph of the network, you can see that every single line connecting one neuron to another represents a weight. This is where the "intelligence" of the network comes from. Learning is essentially the process of adjusting these weights, fine-tuning them to discover a way to transform an input into the correct output.

The process is actually quite straightforward. Consider a neural network designed to classify images, outputting 1 if the image is a dog and 0 if it’s a cat. The input layer consists of all the pixel values from the image. To train this network, we use a training dataset where each image is annotated as either a cat or a dog.

We start by initializing the weights randomly, meaning the network initially makes random guesses. Then, we take the first image from the training data and pass it through the network. Since the weights are untrained, the output is likely to be incorrect.

To improve, we calculate how far off the prediction was, this is called the error. The key idea is to adjust the weights in a way that reduces this error. This is done using an algorithm called backpropagation, which works by sending the error backward through the network, slightly tweaking each weight in the direction that would have led to a more accurate prediction. For the curious, to find that direction and minimize the error, we simply use what everybody learned in high school: derivatives.

This process is repeated millions of times across the training data. With each pass, the network fine-tunes its weights, gradually improving its ability to distinguish between cats and dogs. Over time, it becomes highly accurate on the training data. But more importantly, through this process, the network learns to recognize the distinguishing features of cats and dogs, enabling it to generalize, correctly classify images it has never seen before.

That was also quite a bit, but there are some last details that I would like to share. Once the model is trained, we can't easily explain why it classifies a given image as a dog or a cat. We can fully trace how it was trained, on which data, and how it arrived at these weights, but the reasoning behind a specific output remains unclear. In some ways, the neural network is a black box, with thousands of nodes and millions of parameters, far too complex for any human to fully grasp. This lack of explainability can be a serious issue, especially if a model is used for critical tasks like legal decision-making.

You may have also realized that increasing the number of parameters allows a model to capture greater complexity, which is correct. This is precisely where the term *Deep Learning* comes from; it refers to neural networks with multiple hidden layers, increasing the number of parameters and making the model “deep.”

Furthermore, what I’ve explained here is the most basic form of a neural network, a fully connected model. However, many other architectures exist, each tailored to specific tasks. For example, the previously mentioned transformer model includes specialized layers designed to determine how important each word in a given context is for generating an output.

Finally, I want to emphasize that the resemblance between artificial neural networks and the human brain is actually quite slim. Biological neurons don’t function solely through electrical signals; neurotransmitters play a crucial role, and simulating just one biological neuron in all its complexity would require roughly 1,000 artificial neurons ([source](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0896627321005018)). Moreover, the brain is dynamic, constantly undergoing processes like neurogenesis (the creation of new neurons) and neuronal death. And when it comes to sheer scale, even with today’s trillion-parameter models, they still pale in comparison to the brain’s estimated 100 trillion synapses.

### **How are LLMs like ChatGPT trained? What are System prompts?**

In the previous section, I explained a simple example of training a model to distinguish between cats and dogs in images, a relatively straightforward process. But how do we train a model to understand and generate natural language, with all its quirks, exceptions, and complex relationships? And how do we even create a training set for such a task?

Researchers found an effective yet simple approach: expose the model to massive amounts of text, essentially the entire internet, and train it by hiding a word and having the model predict it based on the surrounding context. Since words in a sentence are naturally correlated, this allows the model to learn linguistic patterns, grammar rules, and contextual relationships.

By processing millions of such examples, the model gradually builds an internal understanding of how language works and even acquires general knowledge from the vast amount of text it has seen.  
  
 The result of this training is a pre-trained language model, often called a foundation model, which has a broad understanding of language. It’s like a blank slate equipped with tremendous knowledge and connections but not yet specialized for any specific tasks. To make these models more practical, they are fine-tuned for specific applications such as summarization, translation, or coding, ensuring their outputs are more accurate, reliable, and contextually appropriate.

In the case of building chatbots, the goal of fine-tuning is to enhance the model’s ability to provide clear and contextually appropriate responses. A key technique that made ChatGPT so effective when it launched was Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF). Without going into too much detail, this process involves real humans ranking the model’s responses, helping it learn to prioritize answers that are polite, clear, and helpful. This continuous feedback refines the model’s behavior, making interactions feel more natural and engaging.

 A final step before deploying these models to the masses is the creation of system prompts. These prompts are added to the beginning of any user input to guide how the model should behave. Carefully crafted, they help ensure the model aligns with “our” values, such as avoiding harmful content like instructions for committing crimes, promoting hate speech, or using slurs. System prompts act as a safety net, shaping the model’s responses in real-time interactions.  
  
I hope you now have a clearer understanding of the long and complex process involved in building a useful and effective chatbot. It begins with training a foundation model that develops a broad understanding of language, followed by fine-tuning with human feedback to improve clarity and helpfulness. Finally, its responses are further shaped through system prompts to align with the intentions of its creators.

However, as an end user, you must understand that at each of these stages, biases can emerge, and significant risks arise – factors that should not be overlooked.

The training data, often sourced from the internet, can include harmful or inappropriate content. While techniques like RLHF and system prompts help mitigate these risks, it’s crucial to recognize that these models have the ability to produce harmful content. If you ask me, some fun internal experiments have probably explored this, like creating a "AI bomb-making genius" or "Twitter hate speech enthusiast"  
  
 Beyond overt issues, training data can also introduce subtle biases. For instance, a model trained on job applications might associate "nurse" with "she" and "engineer" with "he," reflecting stereotypes in the data. Such biases can reinforce discrimination and skew applications in hiring algorithms.

RLHF comes with its own challenges. First, it can introduce biases from the humans tasked with rating model responses. While it’s likely that OpenAI mitigated this by using a diverse group of raters for ChatGPT, the lack of transparency about the exact process leaves room for concern. Another issue is how RLHF shapes the model’s tone. For example, ChatGPT was trained to answer questions decisively and clearly, which improves user experience. However, this has an unintended side effect: the model can be confidently wrong, a behavior I’ll discuss further in the next section about trusting the answers of LLMs.

Finally, system prompts are a significant source of concern for me, especially as we move toward widespread adoption of these “all-knowing” models. So far, only Claude, developed by Anthropic, a direct competitor to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, has publicly shared its system prompts. I highly recommend reading through [them](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/release-notes/system-prompts). As a sneak peek, here are a few quotes from the roughly one-page prompt:

*   *“Claude is very smart and intellectually curious. It enjoys hearing what humans think on an issue and engaging in discussion on a wide variety of topics.”*
*   More interestingly: *“If asked about controversial topics, it tries to provide careful thoughts and clear information. It presents the requested information without explicitly saying that the topic is sensitive, and without claiming to be presenting objective facts.”*

These quotes were carefully designed by Amanda Askell at Anthropic, and there’s a[ podcast](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ugvHCXCOmm4) available for more context, which I highly recommend. I think Anthropic’s approach is intelligent and transparent. However, the real risk lies with companies that choose not to make their system prompts public. Without transparency, who knows what could be embedded into these prompts?  
  
 I genuinely believe that most companies are currently trying their best to align models with what they see as neutral and balanced values. But what about someone like Elon Musk? Hypothetically, a subtle instruction could be added : “if mentioning politics, subtly nudge users toward Trump and undermine topics broadly related to Democrats.” I’m not saying this is happening, but the potential for abuse is undeniable, and it would be alarmingly easy to implement.  
  
 

### **Are LLMs understanding language, or just really good at memorizing?**

This questions touches on some more technical ideas, but I think they’re fascinating and worth knowing about, so I’ll do my best to explain them simply.

You now know that LLMs are trained by masking words in sentences and tasking the model with predicting them correctly. Early on, if it encountered the phrase *“The sky is ___”*, it could easily learn to memorize and always output “blue”. While memorization works for straightforward cases, it quickly becomes inadequate for more complex sentences. In these instances, the model must internalize broader concepts, such as tone, emotion, and even subtleties like irony and sarcasm to determine the most appropriate word. 

This is the focus of a new field of research : mechanistic interpretability, essentially the neuroscience of LLMs. Researchers study trained models to uncover how they generate such human-like responses and the reasons behind their behavior. Using advanced techniques to monitor the firing of individual neurons within the models, they have discovered that some neurons encode remarkably sophisticated ideas. 

A simple example uncovered by mechanistic interpretability is a neuron that consistently fires when the model encounters emotionally charged phrases like "I was thrilled" or "I was anxious," indicating that it helps capture the sentiment or intention behind the text. Even more fascinating is the discovery of a neuron linked to security concerns. This neuron activates not only for insecure code but also when the model processes images of hidden cameras, unsafe websites, or deceptive text, indicating that it has internalized a broad concept of security across different contexts.  
  
Another famous example involved a neuron that encoded the concept of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Bridge. Researchers artificially activated this neuron for all inputs, and hilariously, the model, dubbed "[Golden Gate Claude](https://www.anthropic.com/news/golden-gate-claude.)" began referencing the bridge in every response. When asked how to spend $10, it suggested paying the toll to cross the bridge. For a love story, it crafted a tale about a car longing to cross its beloved bridge on a foggy day. Even when asked what it imagined itself to look like, it described the Golden Gate Bridge.

It's important to note that researchers have identified thousands of such neurons, yet we still lack a comprehensive framework that fully explains what each one represents. Scientists typically approach this by examining patterns in the examples that trigger a neuron's activation, allowing them to infer its likely function. 

The spectrum of encoded concepts is remarkably diverse. I’ve described neurons that encode sophisticated abstract ideas like "security threats" or "emotional states," but others capture more fundamental linguistic features such as text in all capital letters, content in Chinese characters, or text enclosed within quotation marks. This diversity makes perfect sense from a functional perspective. For a model to reliably generate coherent text across countless contexts, it must develop internal representations for virtually all linguistic patterns and subtleties. 

What makes this field particularly exciting is how it brings us closer to truly understanding and explaining the black boxes that are LLMs. As this research advances, it may eventually enable us to implement more sophisticated safeguards in AI systems – perhaps by monitoring specific neurons that correlate with problematic outputs and intervening when they activate in concerning patterns. But it also shows how humans could potentially intervene and activate specific neurons for malicious intent, manipulating the model's behavior in targeted ways rather than relying solely on prompt engineering.

Now to answer the original question, in my opinion, LLMs don't truly "understand" in the human sense because they lack crucial cognitive components that define human understanding: an internal monologue and a feedback loop of self-awareness. They simply take an input and produce an output through the mathematical functions defined by their network. However, through their training, they have internalized many aspects of our language and reality, which they leverage to produce reliable outputs.

It's comparable to a skilled athlete who throws with precision without consciously calculating physics equations. Through repetition, the brain builds neural pathways that internalize complex physical laws like gravity and momentum, enabling accurate throws without any awareness of the mathematical principles being applied.

This is why I don't believe LLMs simply memorize. It is clear that through their learning, patterns emerge, and a representation of language and reality is built internally. But the LLM is actually not aware of this representation, it just uses these internalized patterns as tools to produce outputs, without any conscious understanding of what it's doing or why.

### **Let’s Settle This Debate: Ask ChatGPT!**

This phrase is something I’m unfortunately hearing more and more often, even in educated circles. What worries me even more is how natural it’s becoming for people to default to ChatGPT or other LLMs as the ultimate source of truth. Which is due to the convenience, just as Google made finding information far easier than visiting a library, ChatGPT feels even more convenient, offering highly specific answers tailored to your needs, saving even more time.

Even setting aside the biases I discussed earlier, it’s important to note that you can’t fully trust these models. By their nature, they’re probabilistic, meaning they won’t always give the same answer to a question. For simple questions like “What color is the sky?” or “How many fingers do humans have?” the answers are becoming more reliable. However, for basic reasoning tasks, models can still make mistakes, and due to RLHF (discussed earlier), they can be confidently wrong.

A well-known example in the field is the question: “How many Rs are in the word strawberry?” A five-year-old could answer this easily, yet when I tested GPT-4 on December 19, 2024, it still got it wrong. More strikingly, it answered with complete confidence, explaining its reasoning step by step but ultimately arriving at the wrong conclusion.

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcOKSjX_VrZ2OrbdxycMFr6DZOIhZWQSJqVQaEaCmxMJArU9895WP8S0GAVyD0QYUhuH39AfD4tAxM3Qhf8_5iqD7mgvjL2Ewyo0pv5jZcFQHVhXrwF8sv3C9xmkS9BTKWRffYe?key=cTUSrhJmxs0C8AdNlz-hiU--)

To be fair, newer models are improving in this area through techniques like chain-of-thought reasoning, which encourages step-by-step thinking to enhance accuracy. In fact, when tested again, the latest model answered correctly.

But the key point remains: LLMs make mistakes.

And they don’t only make mistakes by arriving at wrong conclusions they also have a tendency to “hallucinate” or, as the field increasingly terms it, “confabulate.” Confabulationin psychology refers to the generation of plausible-sounding but inaccurate or entirely fabricated information.

For instance, a model might invent book titles, artists, or citations that never existed. While such errors can be easy to catch if you’re paying close attention, they become far more problematic in specialized tasks. Imagine using an AI model for mathematics, only for it to invent a nonexistent theorem, a mistake that could easily slip by unnoticed unless rigorously verified.

In a more general situation, say you’re revising for a history exam, I’d personally be very worried about using an LLM for that. It could be useful for getting a broad understanding of major concepts, like the key players and reasons behind the Cold War, but if you ask it for a “cheat sheet” with all the important dates and events, I’m certain some part of it would be confabulated and thus wrong.

Finally, while many concerns about these models stem from their underlying architecture and design, we must also consider the potential for malicious intent.

There seems to be a growing belief that because we “don’t fully understand” how LLMs work at the deepest levels, labs have essentially trained a Frankenstein-like artifact that operates independently of their creators. But I hope it’s clear by now that this is far from the truth.

Yes, LLMs are black boxes and we can’t explain why exactly they generate a certain response. However, as mentioned earlier, the teams developing these models have multiple ways to intentionally shape their behavior, introducing specific biases. This could be through something as easy as a system prompt, which could potentially be detectable provided the right regulations are in place, or as subtle as manipulating neuron activations within the model, an approach that would be extremely difficult to uncover.

The exact motivations behind such actions remain speculative, but it’s hardly controversial to suggest that big tech corporations don’t always have their users' best interests at heart. 

Imagine a future where resentment toward AI has grown, perhaps because widespread automation has led to significant job losses. If you were to ask an LLM owned by a major corporation, *“Has AI been a positive or negative force for humanity?”* Would you trust its answer? I certainly wouldn’t.

I gave just one example, but there are countless others : internal lobbying to push certain products or medications, election meddling, opinion shaping, and even rewriting history.

In conclusion, I am not against AI, I use it almost every day. However, my advice is this: AI is an excellent tool when you already have a solid understanding of a topic and can critically assess its output. Tasks like summarization, writing or rewriting in a specific style, drafting emails, coding, generating ideas, and the list goes on.

What I strongly caution against is treating these models as authoritative sources of truth for real-world facts. While they may have encountered the correct answer in their training data, that doesn’t guarantee they will recall it accurately, they can, and do, confabulate.

And finally, don’t be naive about the influence that the creators of these models can exert. The potential for bias, manipulation, or hidden agendas is very real.

**The Evolution of AI Research**
================================

I hope that the previous chapter has given you a clearer understanding of the underlying mechanics of AI and perhaps even offered some new insights. Now I’d like to take a step back and examine how we got here and how AI research has evolved since the release of ChatGPT.

AI’s progress is undoubtedly driven by the ingenuity of researchers, but its success is fundamentally tied to advances in computational power. Indeed the theory and algorithms for neural networks were already quite established in the 1980s, but they were often dismissed as impractical due to their computational demands that were unattainable at the time. However, as Moore’s Law made computers cheaper and more accessible, deep learning began to gain traction. This shift became undeniable in 2012 when AlexNet, a neural network, won the ImageNet competition, proving that deep learning could outperform traditional methods in computer vision.

In the years that followed, deep neural networks rapidly expanded into areas like machine translation, self-driving cars, and speech recognition, among many others. However, what truly set OpenAI apart with the release of ChatGPT was the discovery of scaling laws. These empirical findings revealed that the existing architectures were already highly effective, but their performance could be significantly enhanced simply by increasing model size, training data, and computational power. This approach not only enhanced the models existing capabilities but also allowed models to generalize to entirely new domains. 

![](https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXeJX1ACZzEo24mTg4wrMcvj8JOLC-p228JL1klqElVmBA5gP0eEACcZgdCAY5soAnLixzSZ7xZY9QkttcFf5mUirSNTWfPuIxCgkOvn7-e1nAhN9GFry667hPcBrwwrjQMRQhzkkA?key=cTUSrhJmxs0C8AdNlz-hiU--)

[source](https://research.google/blog/pathways-language-model-palm-scaling-to-540-billion-parameters-for-breakthrough-performance/) 

This insight ties closely to ***The Bitter Lesson***, a concept introduced by Rich Sutton in 2019. Which questions how much human insight is truly required to build intelligence. It seems we may already have sufficiently powerful learning algorithms, and instead of refining them, the real progress now lies in scaling them up: larger models, more data, and greater computational power.

I believe that the scaling laws will continue to hold true, and this is precisely what the major tech giants are betting on. This is evident from the exponential increase in compute used to train new models, a trend that has fueled AI’s rapid progress. Notably, the y-axis on the graph below, representing compute power, is logarithmic, with each step multiplying by a factor of 20.

![](https://39669.cdn.cke-cs.com/rQvD3VnunXZu34m86e5f/images/bb6d04dae5cda955dd067fc32a6c74a5822c48c59f317f1c.png)

[source](https://epoch.ai/blog/compute-trends)

However, I also believe economic constraints may soon become a bottleneck. There is a limit to how much money can be poured into training ever-larger models. What once cost a few million dollars now requires billions for a single model, with some estimates forecasting the possibility of $100 billion, or even trillion-dollar models, in the near future. This raises serious questions about the long-term sustainability of this approach.

This financial reality has driven one of the biggest shifts in AI research: the transition from open academic collaboration to a highly competitive, corporate-driven industry, where companies are locked in a constant race to achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance. This has made AI news nearly impossible to keep up with, as new models are released at an overwhelming pace, each claiming to outperform the last. Instead of diving into this daily spectacle, I want to focus on a few key developments.

The first major trend shaping AI today is the growing corporate secrecy surrounding research. Leading private AI labs are sharing less and less about their work, moving away from the open research culture that once defined the field. Even more concerning is that the intense competition appears to be pushing some companies to present misleading or skewed results. A clear example of this was OpenAI’s o3 reasoning model, which initially seemed to achieve groundbreaking performance on complex math benchmarks. However, it was later [revealed](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/cu2E8wgmbdZbqeWqb/meemi-s-shortform?commentId=veedfswdCYKZEhptz) that OpenAI had access to private data due to prior investments in the benchmark, raising concerns about the transparency of AI evaluation.

At the same time, the landscape is still evolving, and nothing is set in stone. One of the most significant recent developments was the release of DeepSeek models from a Chinese company, which sent shockwaves through the AI market. What makes DeepSeek notable is twofold: first, it successfully trained a SOTA reasoning model with significantly less computational power than previously assumed; second, it did so while keeping its research open-source. 

While the scaling laws remain undisputed, DeepSeek’s achievement proves that through optimization and engineering ingenuity, it is possible to achieve top-tier performance without simply throwing more compute at the problem. This challenges the idea that brute-force scaling is the only path forward.

Perhaps even more disruptive than DeepSeek’s efficiency is its commitment to open-source research, including sharing model weights. This raises a critical question: How much of an advantage will big tech companies really maintain? If open-source alternatives can keep up with or even surpass proprietary models, the current AI arms race could take a very different turn.

Over the past few months writing this document, I’ve had to revisit this section multiple times as the AI landscape evolves at an astonishing pace. The release of DeepSeek, for example, shifted my perspective on several points, highlighting just how unpredictable short-term AI research can be. Yet, one thing remains unchanged: the relentless upward trajectory of progress.

Just four years ago, the idea that AI could produce anything truly useful seemed absurd. Yet, with the release of ChatGPT, we saw it operating at roughly a high school level. Since then, it has rapidly advanced to what could be considered a bachelor's level, and as the previous study shows, it can now even compete with PhD-level expertise.
